plan.why: Spin-off of L1 that sends viewers to today's long-form. It uses the muscle-outcome question format (100 and 131 views) instead of a how-to list. | fact-check: A good funnel concept, but four fixes: (1) Timing. The playbook says funnel Shorts run the day after their long-form, and only once it's live. Schedule S3 for the 20:00 slot on the day after L1 publishes, and use L1's final published title word for word (it may become 'Fiber'). (2) Framing. The SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy measured lean mass, which isn't the same as muscle. It also includes water, organs and connective tissue. Say 'about a quarter of the weight lost was lean mass, which includes muscle'. Never say 'a quarter was muscle'. Take the exact proportion, the substudy group sizes (substudy participants by arm, not SURMOUNT-1's full enrolment) and the 72-week timepoint from the published paper. Give the placebo comparison for context. (3) Variety guard. Earlier Shorts ('Fat or muscle?', 'How to protect your muscle') probably used this same substudy. Lead with the new fact, the 2025 joint advisory's recommendation to prioritise protein when intake drops, and keep SURMOUNT-1 to one supporting line. (4) Keep 'recommended by the advisory', never 'proven on tirzepatide'. Include the kidney/protein-limit caveat, 'start strength training gently', one GI line and the prescriber line. Title: two stacked questions are weaker; answer the question within 10 s.

package.title: Eating Less on Tirzepatide? Protein and Muscle, Explained #shorts
package.description:
Follow @InforMedLab for more on eating well on tirzepatide.

On tirzepatide (Mounjaro), appetite — and protein intake — can drop too. In SURMOUNT-1's body-scan substudy of adults with obesity, or overweight plus a related condition, without diabetes, about a quarter of the weight lost with tirzepatide (all doses combined) over 72 weeks was lean mass, which includes muscle, similar to placebo. Digestive side effects like nausea were most common in SURMOUNT-1, mostly mild to moderate.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate and safe. I checked every claim against the cited sources and all of them hold up. The joint advisory is real: it was released on 30 May 2025 by ACLM, ASN, OMA and The Obesity Society, and published in Obesity 2025;33(8):1475–1503 (DOI 10.1002/oby.24336). The free full-text copy on PMC (PMC12125019) confirms it recommends prioritizing protein from varied foods (beans, dairy, seafood, eggs, poultry) and pairing protein with structured strength training. The SURMOUNT-1 body-scan (DXA) study is also correct as written: 124 people on tirzepatide (5, 10 and 15 mg combined) and 36 on placebo, adults with obesity or overweight and no diabetes, measured at week 72. About 26% of the weight lost was lean mass on tirzepatide and about 25% on placebo, so "about a quarter" and "placebo's split was similar" are accurate. The digestive side-effect line matches the SURMOUNT-1 paper in NEJM (2022). The kidney-disease protein caveat, the "start gently" line and the full prescriber line are all there. The narration is about 169 words, inside the 170 limit. The title and hook are paid off by about 10 s. The two issues below are optional wording fixes, not blockers. The Wiley page blocks automated fetches, but the search result and the PMC copy both confirm the reference.

issues.claim: When appetite drops, protein can drop too.
issues.problem: This is a general claim with no source tag. The joint advisory does warn that eating less on GLP-1 therapy can risk not getting enough nutrients, so it supports the line. The wording is already suitably cautious ('can').
issues.fix: Set source_ids for s2 to ["src1", "src1b"]. Keep the narration as it is.

issues.claim: About a quarter of the tirzepatide group's weight loss over 72 weeks was lean mass... Placebo's split was similar.
issues.problem: The proportions are correct (about 26% vs 25%). But the tirzepatide group lost much more weight overall, so they lost more lean mass in absolute terms. A muted viewer who sees only 'similar split' could miss that. This is optional context, not an error.
issues.fix: Optional: change on_screen_text to "Placebo: similar share (about 1 in 4)". Keep the narration as written.
